tip: Mount named volumes with 'docker run -v mydata:/app/data'. Unlike bind mounts, named volumes are managed by Docker and portable across hosts.

title: Pull an image
description: Download an image from a registry to the local Docker image cache — runs automatically before docker run if the image is not present.

breakdown.meaning: Download an image from a registry
Image name and tag

flags.description: Pull image for a specific platform e.g. linux/amd64

example:
docker pull nginx:latest
docker pull node:20-alpine
docker pull ubuntu:22.04
output:
latest: Pulling from library/nginx
Status: Downloaded newer image for nginx:latest
tip: Always pin specific tags (nginx:1.25.3) rather than 'latest' in production to ensure reproducible deployments. Use 'docker pull --platform' for cross-arch images.

title: Stop a running container
description: Gracefully stop a running container by sending SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a timeout — preserves data written to named volumes.

breakdown.meaning: Gracefully stop a running container
Container name or ID

flags.description: Seconds to wait before killing (default 10)

example:
docker stop my-container
docker stop $(docker ps -q)
tip: Use 'docker stop -t 0' to kill immediately without waiting. 'docker stop $(docker ps -q)' stops all running containers in one command.

title: Remove containers
description: Remove one or more stopped containers and free up their storage — containers must be stopped first unless using the -f flag.

breakdown.meaning: Remove one or more containers
Container name or ID

flags.description: Force remove a running container
Also remove associated anonymous volumes

example:
docker rm my-container
docker rm -f my-container
docker rm $(docker ps -aq)
tip: Use 'docker rm $(docker ps -aq)' to remove all stopped containers. Run 'docker system prune' for a full cleanup of images, networks, and build cache.

title: Remove images
description: Remove one or more images from the local Docker image cache to free up disk space — images in use by containers cannot be removed.

breakdown.meaning: Remove one or more images
Image name:tag or image ID

flags.description: Force removal even if a container uses the image

example:
docker rmi nginx:latest
docker rmi $(docker images -q)
tip: Use 'docker image prune -a' to remove all images not used by any container. Tag images with version numbers before pushing to avoid losing track of what 'latest' contains.

title: Live resource usage
description: Stream real-time CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O statistics for running containers — useful for identifying resource-hungry containers.

breakdown.meaning: Display a live stream of container resource usage

flags.description: Report a single snapshot then exit

example:
docker stats
docker stats --no-stream
docker stats my-container
output:
CONTAINER   CPU %  MEM USAGE / LIMIT   NET I/O
nginx       0.1%   12MiB / 1.9GiB    1kB / 2kB
tip: Use '--no-stream' for a one-time snapshot: 'docker stats --no-stream'. Format output with '--format' to show only the columns you need.
